rejected_rule.statement: An Attorney-at-Law shall not accept any professional matter in respect of which he knows or has reason to believe that he would be required as a witness.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: An Attorney-at-Law shall not accept any professional matter in respect of which he knows or has reason to believe that he would be required as a witness. The same principle would apply where an Attorney-at-Law after accepting any professional matter finds that he would be required as a witness in the same matter: Provided, however, an Attorney-at-Law may accept any professional matter in which he may be required only as a witness in respect of any formal non-contentious matter.
rejected_rule.statute_citation_verbatim: Rule 12 of the Supreme Court (Conduct of and Etiquette for Attorneys-at-Law) Rules 1988
